messages:
Grace O'Connor: Dropping the first pass of the PLG signal sequences here (rate-limit pain, spend growth, security intent). Would love SDR eyes before we push into HubSpot sequences. Doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pLgSignalsSeqDrafts (comment mode is on)

Rohan Mehta: :eyes: read through. Overall tone is good, but I’m worried we’re over-asserting a bunch of infra stuff we can’t know.
- Example: “saw you’re running on k8s / autoscaling GPUs” — we don’t know that.
- Example: “we can swap you off vLLM” — we don’t know they’re using vLLM.
- The “your GPU costs are too high” line could annoy ppl.

Rohan Mehta: Biggest ask: add 1–2 concrete benchmarks / outcomes so it doesn’t read like generic “we’re faster/cheaper.” Right now it’s a lot of “optimize latency + cost” without proof.

Stephanie Nguyen: +1 to Rohan. The drafts assume a modern infra stack + a specific pain narrative.
We should anchor on the *signal we actually have* (429s, sustained spend, concurrency spikes, security doc engagement) and then ask a clean question.

Grace O'Connor: Super fair. For benchmarks, what’s safe to claim without legal/security freaking out? We have some internal case studies but not sure what’s approved.

Ben Carter: I can help tighten language + make it more “curiosity + proof” vs “we know your stack.”
For the benchmarks: can we reference Redwood-verified perf profiles in a generic way?
Like “teams commonly see X–Y% lower p95 latency on the same model family” with a footnote “depends on model/ctx length.”

Chris Osei: Quick reminder from the pilot guardrails: we should avoid any wording that implies we inspected customer infra. We can say “based on your Redwood usage signals” or “based on observed API usage patterns.”

Rohan Mehta: Yep. Also the rate-limit sequence needs more specificity. Suggest:
- Mention what we saw: “multiple 429s over the last week” / “burst traffic”
- Offer a specific next step: “15 min to review burst patterns + set up dedicated capacity or quota tuning”
- Add an actual number: “we can typically reduce 429s by adjusting batching + capacity policy” (if that’s true)

Markus Klein: On numbers: we can share ranges we’ve been using in calls, but we need to keep them clearly conditional.
Safe-ish examples (with caveats):
- Dedicated PoCs: usually 20–40% better p95 vs shared API at same throughput once we tune batching + cache.
- Cost: depends heavily on context length + output tokens, but we’ve seen ~15–30% lower $/1M tokens when moving from ad-hoc to tuned batching + caching.
- Reliability: biggest win tends to be eliminating burst-related 429s by reserving capacity + setting sane concurrency limits.
Don’t put “guaranteed” anywhere.

Stephanie Nguyen: This is good. Also for “sustained spend” sequence: right now it’s basically “you’re growing, want to talk?”
Could we make the offer more tangible?
- “help you forecast + lock in predictable throughput”
- “talk commit options vs on-demand”
- “recommend Dedicated when concurrency/latency SLOs start to matter”

Grace O'Connor: Great. I’ll revise with:
1) Remove infra assumptions (k8s/vLLM/NVIDIA etc)
2) Add 1–2 benchmark ranges w/ disclaimers + link to a public-ish page if we have one
3) Make CTA more specific per trigger

Ben Carter: For the CTA, I’d also tone down “hop on a call” and make it “happy to share what we see + a couple options.” Better reply rates.
And we should add a single line opt-out (esp for EU) even if HubSpot handles unsub.

Rohan Mehta: Another nit: the personalization tokens are too aggressive. “I noticed your engineers…” etc.
Keep it to company name + the signal.

Chris Osei: If helpful, we can standardize the “signal sentence” across templates:
“Noticed {company} has been hitting rate limits / growing usage on Redwood over the last {7/14} days.”
Then the rest is offer + question.

Markus Klein: + please don’t promise “we can get you into a VPC in a week” in the security sequence. That gets messy.
Better: “can share our SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency options” + ask what their timeline is.

Grace O'Connor: Got it. I’ll push edits today and re-tag you all in the doc comments.
Target is to finalize copy by EOW so David can build the HubSpot sequences.

Stephanie Nguyen: :thumbsup: Once updated, I’ll do a quick pass for tone + objections.

Rohan Mehta: Thanks. If you want, I can run the updated version against a couple real pilot accounts and sanity check “does this sound creepy?”

Grace O'Connor: Yes please. I’ll DM you 3 examples once the edits are in.

Ben Carter: When you’re ready, I’ll also propose A/B subject lines (short + signal-based vs “quick question”).

Grace O'Connor: Perfect. Closing loop after edits.
